subject.title: MEDIA: tokens inside markdown code fences are silently ignored

question: Should fenced legacy `MEDIA:` directives stay non-extracting with a warning, be extracted as attachments, or remain documented as by-design only?
rationale: The current parser intentionally preserves fenced examples as text, but the issue reports a real silent media-delivery failure; extraction versus diagnostics changes the product contract and false-positive behavior.

options.title: Warn Only At Delivery Boundary
options.body: Keep fenced tokens as text, emit one diagnostic warning in the actual outbound delivery path, and land the linked PR after the remaining warning-path repair.

options.title: Extract From Fences
options.body: Treat standalone fenced `MEDIA:` lines as attachments, accepting the risk that code examples can become deliverable media unless a stricter policy is designed.

options.title: Docs Only
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and rely on documentation that legacy `MEDIA:` lines must be standalone plain text.

recommendation.title: Warn Only At Delivery Boundary
recommendation.body: Keep fenced tokens as text, emit one diagnostic warning in the actual outbound delivery path, and land the linked PR after the remaining warning-path repair.

likelyOwner.reason: This account provided the live member review that frames the warning-boundary contract and has adjacent reply-path history.
